title: Bellarmines Ps 106 forgotten God does not prove absolute calf-cult—Scripture calls willful disobedience forgetting God
source_text: XXXV. Leve est etiam quod opponit Bellarminus, ut probabile reddat Israelitas in vitulo non intendisse verum Deum colere, nimirum quod dicuntur obliti Dei servatoris sui, quum vitulum adoraverunt, Psal. 106. Fecerunt vitulum in Horeb & adoraverunt sculptile: & obliti sunt Deum, qui salvavit eos, qui fecit magnalia in Aegypto, mirabilia in terra Cham, terribilia in mari rubro. Etenim in Scriptura illi Deum obliti dicuntur, non solum ex quorum mente fides & cogitatio de Deo prorsus deleta est, sed qui agunt quasi Dei non meminissent, mandatis ejus aperte obluctantes, quantumlibet in verum Deum credere se profitantur. Sic Psal. 50. propheta fures, moechos, & maledicos graviter reprehendit, accusans illos quod Deum obliti sint: quamvis plurimi, qui vitiis ejusmodi indulgent, aliquam de Deo fidem retineant, nec omnem memoriam de Deo exuerint.
pass_a_gloss: Light also is that which Bellarmine opposes, to render it probable that the Israelites in the calf did not intend to cultivate the true God, namely that they are said to have forgotten God their savior when they adored the calf, Ps. 106. They made a calf in Horeb and adored a graven thing: and they forgot God, who saved them, who did great things in Egypt, wonders in the land of Ham, terrible things in the Red Sea. For in Scripture those are said to have forgotten God, not only from whose mind faith and thought of God is utterly deleted, but who act as if they did not remember God, openly struggling against his commandments, however much they profess to believe in the true God. Thus Ps. 50. the prophet gravely reprehends thieves, adulterers, and cursers, accusing them that they have forgotten God: although very many who indulge vices of that kind retain some faith concerning God, nor have they put off every memory of God.
pass_b_english: Bellarmines Ps 106 forgetfulness does not equal atheism about Jehovah.
Scripture also calls thieves and adulterers forgetters of God while they still profess him—same idiom covers calf-cult disobedience.
